editorial:
Imagine trying to navigate the awkwardness of your first crush while dealing with a chaotic home life. You follow Thomas, a 16-year-old boy who just moved to a new town. He is stuck in a tough spot because his older brother, Charlie, has autism and often acts out in ways that embarrass Thomas. While Thomas is just trying to get close to a girl named Jackie, Charlie keeps popping up at the worst times and causing scenes. It feels very real and grounded, capturing that frustrating feeling of loving someone in your family but wishing they would just leave you alone for five minutes so you can have a normal life.

The acting is what really makes this story work, especially the way it shows the tension between the two brothers. You will feel for Thomas, but you will also start to understand Charlie's perspective as the story goes on. It is not a fast-paced movie, but it is an honest look at family struggles. If you are in the mood for a heartfelt drama, you should definitely check this out. It is a perfect pick for a quiet Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: By the end, Thomas stops trying to hide Charlie from the world. He realizes that his brother is a part of him and that Jackie actually accepts Charlie for who he is. Instead of feeling ashamed, Thomas learns to protect and support his brother. The movie wraps up with a feeling of hope, showing that family bonds are more important than fitting in or looking cool in front of other people.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic stories about family and growing up.
